keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 'Principality of Regensberg' polygons sit on Würzburg, Schweinfurt, Bad Kissingen and Tauberbischofsheim (29 cells, 6,0xx km2; none of them touches Regensburg, Aschaffenburg or Wetzlar): they are the Grand Duchy of Würzburg (capital Würzburg, Schweinfurt added 1810, Würzburg page), not Dalberg's principality. The principality of the Regensburg page (capital Regensburg; Aschaffenburg along the Main; Wetzlar per the mediatisation page) is Regensburg plus the Aschaffenburg land, which Cliopatria files under its 'Grand Duchy of Würzburg' row (13 cells around Aschaffenburg and Hanau, 1806-1807). The Regensburg infobox gives no area; the shape's 6,179 km2 cannot be compared. Frankfurt is added from 1806: 'Frankfurt lost its status as a free imperial city in 1806 with the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire. The city was granted to the former archbishop of Mainz, Karl Theodor Anton Maria von Dalberg' (Grand Duchy of Frankfurt page; the Dalberg page: 'the Reichsstadt of Frankfurt was included among his territories' in 1806). Cliopatria's Würzburg-row shape holds no Frankfurt cell (gazetteer: intersect with an 8 km disc at Frankfurt = 0 cells), so the cell is added to the correction. The Frankfurt page calls the 1806 holding 'the Principality of Frankfurt' and the Regensburg page does not mention Frankfurt: the dossier draws all of Dalberg's lands as one state (as it does for Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar). Caveat: the 13-cell Würzburg-row shape has one cell over Hanau (8.82E 50.09N), but the Regensburg page has Dalberg 'granted Hanau and Fulda' only in return for Regensburg in 1810; the grid cannot separate Hanau from the Main lands beside it, so the cell is kept and flagged.

ledger.note: 1803: Dalberg's Principality of Regensburg is created. Infobox 'Created from all five Reichsfrei territories in Regensburg: 27 April 1803'; 'Most of the new principality consisted of the territory of the former Prince-Bishopric of Regensburg'; Dalberg 'also acquired the Principality of Aschaffenburg'. The mediatisation page: the Mainz electorate 'was moved to Regensburg and enlarged with territory including Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar'.

region.text: the former Free Imperial City of Frankfurt, granted to Dalberg in 1806

ledger.note: 1806: Frankfurt passes to Dalberg. 'Frankfurt lost its status as a free imperial city in 1806 with the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire. The city was granted to the former archbishop of Mainz, Karl Theodor Anton Maria von Dalberg', and by 1810 it was among his 'remaining territories' (Frankfurt page); the Dalberg page: 'the Reichsstadt of Frankfurt was included among his territories' in 1806. No month on either page. The Frankfurt page calls the holding 'the Principality of Frankfurt' and the Regensburg page does not name Frankfurt, so that it belongs to this state is the dossier's reading (confidence 2): all of Dalberg's lands are one colour until the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt.

1806: the electorate becomes a principality of the Confederation of the Rhine. The principality 'lost its electoral status in 1806'; the Confederation page lists Regensburg among the founders of 12 July 1806 and the Regensburg page has it a member 'until 1810'.

region.text: Dalberg's remaining lands that pass to the new state: Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar (his from 1803) and Frankfurt (his from 1806); Fulda and Hanau were added by the grand duchy in 1810

ledger.note: 1810: the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt is formed. 'established on 16 February 1810'; after Dalberg 'was forced by Napoleon to relinquish his Principality of Regensburg to the Kingdom of Bavaria in 1810', 'his remaining territories of Aschaffenburg, Wetzlar, Fulda, Hanau, and Frankfurt were combined' into the grand duchy (Frankfurt page). Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar were Dalberg's from 1803 and Frankfurt from 1806 (the 1806 gain above), so they pass to the new state with this region; only Hanau and Fulda are new in 1810: the Regensburg page says 'In return for conceding Regensburg, Dalberg was granted Hanau and Fulda', gains of the new state, not of this one. (The 13-cell Cliopatria Aschaffenburg shape has one cell over Hanau that the grid cannot separate from the Main lands beside it; it stays in the region.)

region.text: Regensburg, 'formally incorporated' into Bavaria on 22 May 1810

ledger.note: 1810: Regensburg passes to Bavaria. Infobox 'Ceded to Bavaria: 6 January 1810'; Dalberg 'conceded Regensburg to the Kingdom of Bavaria', which 'formally incorporated the city on 22 May 1810' (linked to the Treaty of Paris of 1810).

region.text: the last of Dalberg's principality, the Regensburg territory

ledger.note: 1810: the Principality of Regensburg ends with the incorporation of Regensburg into Bavaria on 22 May 1810; its Main and Lahn lands had already become the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt on 16 February.

certainty.note: Four separate territories (Regensburg, the Aschaffenburg land on the Main, Wetzlar and, from 1806, Frankfurt); no opened page gives a boundary, so the cells are approximate.

notes:
MIS-LABELLED CLIOPATRIA ROWS (the main finding): the four 'Principality of Regensberg' shapes (1806-1813) lie on Würzburg, Schweinfurt, Bad Kissingen and Tauberbischofsheim (the Grand Duchy of Würzburg, 23 Sept 1806 to 3 June 1814), and the 'Grand Duchy of Würzburg' row's 1806-1807 shapes lie on Aschaffenburg and Hanau while its 1811-1814 shapes are the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt. The two rows' names look swapped. All four shapes are verdict 'wrong' here; corrections point at the other row's shapes by Cliopatria name. The eu-20 Würzburg writer should take the 'Principality of Regensberg' polygons as Würzburg's.
ASCHAFFENBURG: the electorate-of-mainz dossier (another group) names a separate 'principality-of-aschaffenburg' as a successor, and the Frankfurt page lists a 'Principality of Aschaffenburg' as a related state. Following the mediatisation page (Dalberg's electorate 'enlarged with territory including Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar') this dossier keeps Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar inside the principality; if a separate Aschaffenburg dossier is written the Aschaffenburg part of the keyframes should move there. Regensburg itself is under 253 km2 of land plus enclaves: a 15 km radius is a placeholder.
OPEN: no area on the Regensburg infobox; Wetzlar and Aschaffenburg are not gazetteer places (lon/lat radius and the Cliopatria 1807 'Grand Duchy of Würzburg' shape are used); the Regensburg page links the 1810 cession to the Treaty of Paris (1810) but gives no treaty date; 6 January (cession) and 22 May 1810 (incorporation) are both on the page and the later is used; Dalberg's years as Prince of Regensburg are on neither the Regensburg nor the Dalberg page: the one ruler entry uses the state's own years (see its note). Page budget 5: Regensburg, Würzburg, Frankfurt, mediatisation, Confederation of the Rhine.
NEEDS A DOSSIER: grand-duchy-of-frankfurt (16 Feb 1810 to Dec 1813), possibly principality-of-aschaffenburg.
FRANKFURT (added in the repair): the Frankfurt page has the city granted to Dalberg in 1806 and among his remaining territories in 1810, and calls the 1806 holding 'the Principality of Frankfurt'; the Regensburg page never mentions Frankfurt. The dossier still draws Frankfurt as Dalberg's land inside this state from 1806 (confidence 2, /ledger/1; the Frankfurt cell is in the 1806 and 1807 keyframes and in the 1810 split region), the same reading as for Aschaffenburg and Wetzlar. holy-roman-empire-minor-states has no matching 1806 loss of Frankfurt (nor the 1803 loss of Regensburg). HANAU: the 13-cell Cliopatria shape that stands for the Aschaffenburg land has a cell over Hanau (8.82E 50.09N) although the Regensburg page grants Hanau to Dalberg only in 1810; kept because the grid cannot separate it from its neighbours.
AFTER MAY 1810: nothing is drawn under this slug (identity.end 1810/5). The 1811 and 1812 corrections point at Cliopatria's 'Grand Duchy of Würzburg' rows only to say that those shapes are the land of grand-duchy-of-frankfurt (to December 1813).
